caption: The drawing depicts a single, curved object resembling a powder horn, centered vertically on a plain, off-white background. The horn tapers to a rounded point at the top, which is decorated with a series of engraved or carved horizontal bands near the neck. The main body of the horn is light tan, varying in hue, with darker shading at the tip and base. The surface is intricately decorated with finely detailed black line work, featuring an arrangement of symbols, patterns, and emblematic designs, including circular motifs, crosshatching, ornamental scrolls, and what appear to be heraldic symbols such as a crown and a ribbon. There is a compass rose and a segment of the map visible towards the lower part of the horn, and additional decorative elements fill the rest of the visible area. The background is plain and free of detail or shading except for some minor, random brown spots scattered across the paper. The text “Lith. Turner” is present near the lower right, indicating the artist or lithographer.
title: Powder Horn
